Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull has reshaped the airflow around the sidepods – the new inlet, matching tweaks to the engine cover and floor, and a re‑shaped rear‑corner vent – to clean up and accelerate the air reaching the car’s rear. The tighter, more efficient flow should boost down‑force and keep the power unit cooler on the high‑speed, high‑heat circuit, giving the team a stronger grip and more consistent performance right out of the gates.

Scuderia Ferrari.summary: Ferrari has trimmed the exit opening of the front brake duct and reshaped the front‑floor fairing, which together clean up the airflow under the nose. The tweaks give the car a bit more grip and a more stable front end, so drivers should feel a smoother, more predictable handling package on the upcoming circuit. This extra aerodynamic efficiency could be the edge they need to fight for podium spots this weekend.

Williams Racing.summary: Williams has introduced new front‑suspension claddings that wrap more tightly around the updated suspension parts, giving the car a cleaner, more efficient package. The tighter fit reduces drag and improves front‑end stability, helping the team extract a little extra grip on the weekend’s circuits. In short, it’s a modest aerodynamic gain that could translate into better lap times and a stronger start off the line.

Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has trimmed the third element of the front wing and shortened the accompanying strake, while also lifting the outer edge of the front‑wing end‑plate and re‑shaping the floor’s leading‑edge devices. These tweaks clean up the airflow over the front of the car and boost the low‑down‑force “ground‑effect” from the floor, giving the car more rear‑end stability and cornering grip. In short, the changes should translate into faster lap times and a more predictable feel for the drivers this weekend.

Haas F1 Team.summary: The Haas front wing now has a simpler actuation system, letting the team shrink the wing’s exposed parts for smoother airflow. This gives the car a cleaner aerodynamic package, improving grip and straight‑line speed just in time for the weekend’s qualifying and race.

Alpine F1 Team.summary: Alpine has given the front of the car a fresh “nose‑flap” that smooths the air hitting the front tyres, helping the car stick to the corner entry a bit better. At the back, the rear‑wing pods and endplates have been reshaped, tightening the airflow and adding a little extra bite without adding drag. The net result should be more stable cornering and a stronger finish line push, giving the team a clearer advantage on this weekend’s track.

Cadillac.summary: Cadillac has refined the rear of the car – the diffuser fence now has a cleaner lower edge and the central diffuser’s trailing edge has been reshaped. Those modest‑looking tweaks tighten the airflow under the car, giving a boost in rear down‑force and making the chassis feel more planted in fast corners. In short, the car should stick to the asphalt better this weekend, translating into quicker lap times and stronger defense on the straights.
